mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate at 0.2% is at or near the zero lower bound, which historically compresses discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction is fixed as positive due to the current low rate environment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1%.

mechanism_narrative: The unemployment rate at 3.6% is below the natural rate, signaling a tight labor market that supports corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and the direction is fixed as positive due to the current low unemployment.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% within a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year rise in CPIAUCSL above 3.0% signals accelerating inflation that leads to central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% and year-over-year CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, it signals a dual threat of monetary tightening and inflation acceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), strong labor market conditions support corporate earnings growth and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is below 105 and housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1750, it signals a strong housing sector that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 105 and HOUST > 1750.

mechanism_narrative: In strong GDP growth regimes (GDPC1 quarterly growth > 1.0% annualized), robust economic expansion supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 quarterly growth exceeds 1.0% annualized.
